blocks.text: Pițipoancă (sometimes shortened to Piți and plurally, Pițipoance) is a slang term used in Romania to describe a subculture of women who stereotypically wear revealing clothes in bright colors or animal prints, high platform shoes often sporting a dark fake tan, "bad" makeup and plastic surgery. The fashion was mainly inspired by the McBling aesthetic. By the late 2010s this style had died almost completely, with the term hitting its peak in mainstream popularity around the late 2000s to the early 2010s, usually used in a derogatory way towards members of the subculture by the media.
Behavioral Tropes: The stereotype portrays these women as obsessed with shopping, frivolous and prone to boasting about status symbols or gifts obtained from wealthy male admirers.

Social Perception: The term is misogynistic and classist, typically utilized by the general public and mainstream media to mock working-class women often perceived as uneducated, superficial, or vain.
Aesthetic: Heavy use of "bad" makeup, bleached or dyed hair, dark spray tans, and an affinity for plastic surgery or artificial cosmetic procedures.
Footwear: Very high platform heels or shoes
Clothing: Tight, bright colors, revealing outfits, and animal prints.
Fashion: Drew inspiration heavily from the mid-2000s Y2K and Mcbling glamour trends.
